title: IF YOU ONLY KNEW…
paragraphs: The King was finally entering His city.

Crowds shouting.
Palms waving.
Prophecy unfolding in plain sight.
In Gospel of Luke 19:41–44, as Jesus Christ approaches Jerusalem, the noise of celebration fades behind a moment that feels almost unbearable.

Not quiet sadness.
Not polite emotion.
This is the grief of rejected love.
“If you, even you, had only known on this day what would bring you peace…” (Luke 19:42)

The Prince of Peace was right in front of them.
Yet their hearts were blind.

They had the temple.
The sacrifices.
The Scriptures.
But when God Himself walked their streets…
Some scholars interpret this moment as one of the most profound expressions of divine compassion in Scripture. The Son of God isn’t cold toward sinners.
Jesus isn’t angry that people need grace.
He grieves when they refuse it.

Enemies surrounding the city.
Walls collapsing.
Children crushed within the ruins.
History records that in AD 70, the Siege of Jerusalem by the Roman Empire devastated the city—exactly as Jesus warned.
The prophecy is spoken through tears.
God does not delight in judgment.
Before the empty tomb, He mourned for the lost.
This is not the cold face of religion.
This is love wounded by rejection.
How many today still miss the moment of God’s visitation?
Yet the same Jesus who cried over Jerusalem still calls today.
With open arms marked by nails.

Blind.
Proud.
Lost in our own peace plans.

He carried our sin to the cross.
He rose again in victory.
And the tears of Luke 19 lead directly to the redemption of Calvary.
If you only knew what brings you peace.

Turn to Him.
Trust Him.
Receive the mercy Jerusalem refused.
And you will discover the truth:

The Savior who wept for sinners
also died for them.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
